zoe (devex): Quick thread: onboarding sampleapp hit a duplicate-charge bug when we combined aggressive retry after 429s with an auth refresh. Wanted SDK input on recommended backoff/jitter + replay safeguards.

ryan (sdk): Short Qs: what do you persist for resume and how are you handling 429?

zoe (devex): We persist a pending object in localStorage containing body + idempotencyKey and we retry on 429 with a tight exponential backoff + small jitter. On reload we re-POST the stored body immediately.

parul (platform): Two triggers for duplicates: (A) token refresh race (original resolves late) and (B) client hammering after 429 with too-small jitter so two attempts slip through. Combined you can create two resources.

ryan (sdk): Agreed. Best practices: 1) don't persist raw bodies (PII risk + replay surface), persist only minimal metadata (idempKey, endpoint, resourceHint). 2) on 429 implement full jitter (rand(0, base)) or capped randomized backoff to avoid synchronized bursts. 3) treat 202 as in-flight; prefer idempotency lookup/polling over blind re-POST.

zoe (devex): For (3) do you mean a HEAD /idemp/:key or polling a status endpoint?

ryan (sdk): Either. Prefer a dedicated idempotency-check: HEAD /resources/idemp/{key} returning 200 (complete), 202 (in-progress), 404 (missing). SDK could add `sdk.idempotency.check(key)` helper. If backend lacks that, poll resource status if you have an id.

parul (platform): Also recommend including a client namespace in the idempotency key (e.g., `appInstance:uuid:key`) so servers can keep dedupe windows scoped. And servers should support an `X-Original-Idempotency` header to help reconciling recreated attempts.

zoe (devex): About auth refresh: our current flow replays immediately after refresh completes. That seems to collide with original late responses. Any guidance?

ryan (sdk): SDK suggestion: emit `auth:refresh:start` and `auth:refresh:end` events. The resume logic should subscribe and: when a refresh starts, delay replays for a grace window (configurable; default 1500ms). After that, call `checkIdempotency` before re-POSTing. Also cap replay attempts (max 3).

parul (platform): For 429s specifically: if you get 429 and token refresh is happening, increase backoff base (multiply by 2) to favor letting inflight ops settle. Avoid exponential bursts after refresh. Use full jitter to spread retries.

zoe (devex): Sounds good. We'll change sampleapp to persist metadata only, add auth event hooks, and switch to full jitter for 429 retries. Can SDK expose helpers to reduce copy/paste?

ryan (sdk): Yes, I'll propose `sdk.resumeSafely(pending)` and `sdk.idempotency.check(key)` in the JS SDK. resumeSafely will: subscribe to auth events, wait grace window if refresh in-flight, call checkIdempotency, if in_progress poll status, if missing create new attempt with a new key and include `X-Original-Idempotency` header. I'll open an RFC+PR for the helper and add examples.

parul (platform): Add a note to quickstart about jitter flavors: full jitter recommended over no-jitter or linear jitter when client fleet size is unknown. Also document server dedupe window expectations.

ci-bot: CI: sampleapps/onboarding #552 triggered tests :runner:

zoe (devex): I'll implement change in sampleapp, add an e2e that simulates 429 + token rotation, and tag PR "sdk-jitter-idempotency".

ryan (sdk): Awesome. When PR lands I'll add a short snippet in the SDK docs showing the resumeSafely pseudocode and a recommended backoff table.

parul (platform): One more edge: if backend returns 200 for both original and replay because it doesn't honor idempotency, clients should still avoid blind replays. We should warn in docs that server support is required for strong guarantees.

zoe (devex): Noted. Thanks all :thumbsup:
